div.p: C.K. Cumming thanks Leonard Woolf for the offer of the post of manager at the Hogarth Press. He explains that, given the hours, the salary and his wish to keep the option of leaving at one month's notice, he is in effect declining it.

address.addrLine:
The Hogarth Press,
The Hogarth Press was founded in 1917 by Leonard and Virginia Woolf.

div.p:
Thank you very much for your letter of the 20th.
January, offering me the post of Manager. I am sorry not to have
replied before, but I have been giving the question very careful
consideration.

The idea has appealed to me strongly and I felt last
week that the fascination and interest of the work would outweigh
other considerations. I like many-sided work, have a passion for
detail, and do not object to a considerable amount of drudgery.
But, as I thought about the matter, I became doubtful, for reasons
that I would like to explain, if I may.

I should feel that I ought to do a considerable
amount of supplementary work, if I could get it. Unfortunately,
the people I wished to consult, seem to have all removed themselves
from London for the moment, and will not be back until next month.
That makes an immediate decision more difficult. But I am rather
afraid that with the hours what they are, it would not be possible
to accomplish the requisite amount in any event. If the post were
a part-time one - even two-thirds time, 10 to 4 - it would be a
different matter.

Knowing myself, I am certain I should never settle
down permanently on a salary of £4 a week for full time, unless I
saw great possibilities in the post itself, which is just what it
is impossible to say without experiment. If I undertook the work
on the proposed terms, the arrangement would, in my mind, be frankly
experimental. There is this further point. I have a number of
friends in book publishing circles and I have thrown out various
lines, from which it is possible, though not probable, that some
offer might result. If, during the first few months, a better post
should unexpectedly be offered me, I should,in all likelihood, want
to accept, for I could not afford to do otherwise. I should wish
to have the option of leaving at one month's notice (which is, in my
view,the usual and most satisfactory period), if I so desired.

What I have said is, I know, tantamount to declining
the post, for you naturally would wish to make arrangements practi-
cally certain to be permanent. I feel sure that you will appreciate
my point of view and the fact that I have tried to be perfectly
candid. I felt that to accept the post with any idea in my mind
that, for the reasons indicated above, I might not wish to remain
permanently, would not be fair to you. I am very sorry indeed
for any delay or waste of time that I may have caused you and
I want to thank you for so kindly offering me the work, which would,
in itself, be highly congenial in every way.
